title: Plan a talk people can follow and remember
course_title: Presentation Skills: Talks, Pitches and Community Meetings

say: Plan a talk people can follow and remember.
This is the video for module one of Presentation Skills.
Most weak talks fail for one reason: the speaker tried to say everything. People leave with a blur of facts and no idea what to do.

say: First, who are they? Women in your cooperative, a supermarket buyer, a grant panel, a ward meeting.

panel.heading: Four questions before you write
items: Who are they?
What do they care about?
What do they already believe?
How much time and attention do they have?

say: What do they care about? A buyer cares about price, supply and quality. A funder cares about impact.

say: What do they already believe? If they think the project failed last year, deal with it early.

say: And how much time will you really get? A chairman may give you five minutes. Plan for that, not the time you hope for.

say: Your main message is the one sentence you want people to repeat at home that evening. Keep it to 20 words or fewer. Our cooperative is doing well is too vague. Support us is a weak action.

panel.heading: Vague or specific?
right: A trial order of 50 packs this week

say: Our cooperative can supply 200 loaves a day to your shop at a steady price from next month. That is a message.
And place a trial order of 50 packs this week is an action people can say yes to today.

panel.heading: Vague or specific?
right: A trial order of 50 packs this week

say: For example, Ngozi runs a tailoring business in Enugu and has 5 minutes at a women's business forum. Her audience is about 40 traders and two bank staff.

panel.heading: Ngozi finds her one message
items: Audience: about 40 traders and 2 bank staff
Want: uniform orders, and to look reliable
Message in 17 words, not 34
Action: give me your number today
Cut what does not support the message

say: She wants traders to order staff uniforms, and the bank staff to see her as a serious borrower.

say: Her first message was 34 words and mixed two ideas. Her final one is 17 words: I make neat, durable staff uniforms in 10 working days, and I can take orders of 50 or more.

say: Her action: give me your number after this session, and I will bring fabric samples to your shop this week.

say: She cuts her electricity complaint and most of her life story. Audiences remember three points much better than seven.

panel.rule: Keep no more than three key points. Cut the rest.

say: Give the opening about 10 to 15 percent of your time. Start with a hook, such as a short true story or a question they care about. Then state your message and a one-line map.

panel.heading: Opening, body and close
items: Opening, 10 to 15 percent: hook, message, map
Body, 70 to 80 percent: two or three points
Close, about 10 percent: message and action

say: The body gets about 70 to 80 percent. Choose a pattern, such as problem, solution, benefit for a pitch, or what, so what, now what for a short update.

panel.heading: Opening, body and close
items: Opening, 10 to 15 percent: hook, message, map
Body, 70 to 80 percent: two or three points
Close, about 10 percent: message and action

say: The close gets about 10 percent. Say to close, repeat your message, and ask for the action clearly. In a 5-minute talk, that is about 45 seconds each for opening and close.

panel.heading: Opening, body and close
items: Opening, 10 to 15 percent: hook, message, map
Body, 70 to 80 percent: two or three points
Close, about 10 percent: message and action
panel.rule: Never end with "That's all". Plan your last sentence.

say: A racing heart and dry mouth are your body's normal stress response. It is getting you ready.

panel.heading: A one-minute breathing routine
items: Feet flat, shoulders down
Breathe in through your nose for 4
Breathe out through your mouth for 6
Repeat 5 to 6 times
Sip water, say your first line quietly

say: Stand with both feet flat and drop your shoulders.

say: Take one sip of water, and say your first sentence quietly to yourself. If your mind goes blank mid-talk, pause, breathe, and look at your key-point card.

panel.rule: Nerves are normal. Manage them, do not fight them.

say: Arrive 30 to 45 minutes early. Know your opening by heart. Charge your devices and save your files offline. Test the sound from where you will stand.

panel.heading: Pre-talk checklist
items: Opening memorised
Devices charged, files offline
Sound and screen tested
Cables taped down, exits known
Phone on Do Not Disturb
Water and a printed back-up

say: Tape cables down so nobody trips. Never overload extension boxes, never touch plugs with wet hands, and if a socket sparks, stop and tell the organiser.

panel.heading: Pre-talk checklist
items: Opening memorised
Devices charged, files offline
Sound and screen tested
Cables taped down, exits known
Phone on Do Not Disturb
Water and a printed back-up

say: Turn on Do Not Disturb so private messages do not pop up on screen, and never show children or savings balances without consent. Bring water and a printed back-up in case the power fails.

say: To remember. Study your audience. Write one message of 20 words or fewer, and one clear action. Keep three key points at most. Breathe in for 4 and out for 6. And check the room early.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Study your audience first
One message of 20 words or fewer
One small, clear action
No more than three key points
Breathe in for 4, out for 6
Check power, sound and cables early
